claims.text: A DBMS maintains a data dictionary that records every table, attribute, key and relationship in the database, so the database describes itself to the system.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A DBMS provides data modelling and a logical schema: the design is stated once as the tables, attributes and relationships the database presents, and the DBMS maps it onto the physical storage, so the storage can change without the design changing.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A DBMS enforces data integrity: constraints such as primary-key uniqueness and referential integrity are checked on every change, so invalid data is refused.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A DBMS provides data security, including backup procedures and access rights granted to individual users and groups, deciding which operations each user may perform.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The developer interface is the DBMS tool a developer uses to create and change the database structure - tables, keys, constraints - and to build forms, queries and reports.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The query processor is the DBMS part that takes a query, checks and optimises it, and carries it out against the database, so applications ask for data in a language rather than navigating the storage.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
